experiment: Paired conditioned training and native launch batching audit

limitations: Diagnostic FP32 gradients at one existing checkpoint, not a causal proof of harmful interference.
Scene/photo groups are content domains for the same renderer loss, not the separate tasks in the PCGrad paper.
No validation images enter this diagnostic. Negative gradient alignment alone does not prove projection will improve quality.

mechanical_tests.scope: One checked scene/photo training pair. Gradient routing and averaging only; no fitting or validation evaluation.

mechanical_test_repeatability_note: The initial ordinary-GPU repeat differed by at most 6.402842700481415e-10 in the averaged FP32 gradient. Deterministic execution made routing and joint-loss averaging exact. Training settings were not changed by this test process.

residual_tests.scope: Finite FP16 patterns in selected operand combinations, not every possible triple.

conditioning_tests.scope: Finite half patterns in selected operand combinations, not every possible combination. Explicit round-to-nearest per operation.

limitations: Finite-input equivalence to existing student arithmetic, not native quality.
Complete student graph timings exclude D3D12 integration and do not accelerate native NVIDIA execution.
Exact full-image results cover only the checked checkpoints, inputs and environment.
Intervals average ten consecutive graph replays; p95 is an interval-average percentile, not per-frame tail latency.
Measured execution of experimental students plus grade, excluding D3D12 integration. No native-runtime acceleration.
One static input and one device; other desktop GPU work is not controlled.

findings: Six uncensored sampled frames each contain 158 successful one-kernel calls and 16 logged global UAV barriers with the same associated markers.
The before_chain marker is set immediately before entering each native launch and remains afterward. Events cannot be classified as inside the launch versus between calls from this field.
The observer records transitions only for registered NR-created buffers, plus selected UAV/aliasing events. It does not record the complete D3D12 command stream.
The last sampled frame is censored by the 4096-event cap and cannot establish a complete barrier schedule.
Summed native-call CPU durations are not GPU overhead or a predicted GPU speedup.
required_evidence_before_batching: An uncapped bounded evaluation trace distinguishing command-list calls inside native launch APIs from calls between them.
Coverage of all commands and resources relevant to ordering, plus owned copies and verified lifetimes of packed launch arguments.
Documented or directly tested chain ordering/memory semantics, followed by paired output equality and end-to-end GPU timing in the isolated sample.

limitations: No native-quality replacement is accepted or installed.
Negative gradient alignment at one checkpoint is not proof of the full harmful-interference conditions in the PCGrad paper.
Both new runs share architecture, data, 4500 optimizer updates and 9000 sampled examples. The original single-example conditioned baseline uses only 4500 examples and different domain weighting.
The prior plain PCGrad reference has fewer parameters and no decoder conditioning; it is an architecture comparison, not the matched projection control.
Only 46 training and 16 validation first-reset frames are used. Validation remains outside fitting but informs research choices; no representative temporal or game acceptance is established.
Existing optional CUDA fusions are checked on the new weights. No new CUDA kernel or native-runtime acceleration is introduced.
Full 1080p student-plus-grade graph timings exclude D3D12 integration. Alternating intervals average ten replays, not individual-frame tail latency.
The native trace audit identifies missing ordering evidence. It does not establish executable batches or a GPU speedup.
No sample or game launch, no game/driver/native model or normal runtime changes.
